currentContext.expansion: The annual report does not disclose a capex programme, project-wise outlay or dated commissioning schedule. Expansion is described as footprint and utilisation rather than new capacity: an end-to-end backward integrated manufacturing ecosystem spanning 43 state-of-the-art global facilities that optimises asset utilisation, ensures supply assurance and maintains proximity to customers while mitigating input cost volatility, with a global presence across more than 140 countries covering manufacturing facilities, field stations, R&D chemistry centres, new Agtech/NPP sites, Global Capability Centres and Advanta in-house and R&D facilities in geographies including the USA, Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Costa Rica, Colombia, Indonesia, India, South Korea, China, the UK, France, Italy, Mauritius, Israel, Ukraine, Hungary, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Australia, Spain, Belgium, Vietnam, Thailand and South Africa. During FY26 the Company established and scaled up three state-of-the-art Global Capability Centres in India, Colombia and Mauritius, consolidating global functions across finance, supply chain, human resources and marketing; these three centres are now fully operational. Capacity growth came from higher utilisation rather than new lines - EBITDA growth was supported by improved contribution margins on account of enhanced capacity utilisation and lower input costs, with the resilient global supply chain optimising capacity utilisation across the manufacturing base alongside inventory optimisation and input cost management. Portfolio/geographic expansion was inorganic and structural rather than greenfield: DECCO was successfully integrated with Advanta, capturing synergies, widening the portfolio and strengthening regional channels; Advanta expanded its global seed franchise and SUPERFORM strengthened its presence in specialty chemicals, with super specialty chemicals expanding across paints, mining, rubber, nutraceuticals and pharmaceuticals. Two structural corporate actions are pending: the proposed IPO of Advanta Enterprises Limited (DRHP filed with SEBI and the Stock Exchanges in January 2026, in-principle approval received on March 12, 2026), and a Composite Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Board on February 20, 2026 to consolidate the India and International Crop Protection businesses into UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions Limited, which is proposed to be independently listed, subject to requisite statutory and regulatory approvals.

risks.risk: Climate change and GHG emissions (energy management)
risks.note: BRSR flags climate change mitigation and energy management as risks with negative financial implications - GHG emissions from the business contribute to global warming, and continued reliance on non-renewable energy leads to higher CO2 emissions and environmental damage. Mitigation is a focus on renewables under a detailed Decarbonisation roadmap.

Improper disposal of hazardous and non-hazardous waste leads to significant regulatory, environmental and social issues and may impose reputational and financial risk; mitigated by recycling and co-processing to reduce waste going to landfill.

Water is a shared resource between communities and the business; responsible consumption, recycling and reuse are essential, addressed through a strategy aimed at minimising the overall water footprint. Flagged with negative financial implications.

risks.risk: Regulatory compliance across a multi-country footprint
risks.note: Non-compliance leads to legal penalties and litigation and reduces trust and brand reputation; the Company relies on regular and periodic reviews of current and upcoming compliance requirements. Relevant given operations and registrations across many jurisdictions.

risks.risk: Process safety and occupational health & safety
risks.note: Process safety concerns prevention of unintentional chemical releases or accidents during manufacturing that could harm people, property or the environment. Most Indian sites are ISO 45001:2018 certified, with additional ISO certifications being considered for all UPL sites.
Counterfeit product can harm customers and the brand; addressed via supply chain controls, inspections and advanced authentication technologies to protect product integrity and consumer safety.

Exports contribute 65.15% of total turnover of the entity, so earnings are structurally exposed to overseas demand, trade dynamics and currency movement - the Board's Report attributes part of FY26 revenue growth to favourable foreign exchange movements.

risks.risk: Sector cyclicality - commodity prices and farm economics
risks.note: The MD&A describes a preceding macro-period of turbulent global commodity prices and widespread farm economics stress, and a challenging macroeconomic environment impacting the global agricultural sector; the business remains exposed to input/output price cycles, mitigated through high-value innovation and product differentiation that de-risk it from legacy commodity price volatility.

Manufacturing of chemical and chemical products accounts for 83.20% of standalone turnover (with wholesale trading at 16.80%), concentrating the standalone entity in a single, heavily regulated product category.

risks.risk: Execution risk on pending corporate restructuring
risks.note: The proposed Advanta IPO and the Composite Scheme of Arrangement consolidating India and international crop protection into UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions Limited are subject to requisite statutory and regulatory approvals, so the intended simplification and value unlocking are not yet certain.

one-line thesis: UPL delivered robust Q2FY23 performance with 18% revenue and 35% EBITDA growth driven by pricing power, product mix optimization, and strong demand in Latin America, North America, and India, while aggressively reducing net debt by $650M through operational cash flow, asset divestments, and buybacks, positioning itself as a margin-leading, debt-reduced global agrochemical player with strategic growth in specialty chemicals and sustainability.
financial scorecard: rev:+18% YoY; EBITDA:+35% YoY; PAT:+28% YoY; orderbook:Strong; netdebt:-$650M target by FY23 end
guidance: FY23 revenue growth: 12-15%; EBITDA growth: 15-18%; effective tax rate: 15-18%; net debt reduction: $650M (incl. $150M buyback); working capital cash conversion: $750-800M in H2
order book & pipeline: Strong, with anticipated robust demand in H2 supported by high commodity prices and product optimization; no explicit order book value provided but implied by guidance and inventory buildup
segment / subsidiary detail: Latin America: 20% growth, 50% of revenue, led by herbicides and Evolution fungicide; North America: 24% growth, strong herbicide pricing and distributor support; Europe: flat revenue (USD), +13% growth (EUR), impacted by euro devaluation; India: 22% growth, driven by glufosinate, new insecticides, NPP Biosolutions, and rabi crop products; Rest of World: 21% growth, led by Southeast Asia, Australia, Southern Africa; Japan flat despite yen devaluation
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion of specialty chemicals platform (INR 14,000 cr revenue base); Kudos Chemie acquisition (INR 237 cr) to boost pharma/beverage intermediates; Advanta Seeds and UPL SAS spin-offs unlocking value; Gigaton Carbon Goal rollout in Africa; new product launches (80+ in FY23); AgTech platform scaling in India
margins & cost dynamics: Contribution margin: 42.6% (+290 bps YoY); EBITDA margin: up 278 bps YoY; driven by pricing (+21%), product mix shift to high-margin products, portfolio rationalization; SG&A as % of sales stable; freight costs down in USD but offset by currency depreciation; employee cost inflation persistent
capex / expansion: Significant Capex directed toward backward integration in India for key raw materials; Kudos Chemie acquisition (INR 237 cr) adds manufacturing capacity; focus on specialty chemicals and sustainability infrastructure; no explicit total Capex figure provided but implied as part of $2B manufacturing platform expansion
capital allocation: Net debt reduction target: $650M (incl. $260M from Advanta/UPL SAS strategic alliances, $150M share buyback, $240M from operations); prioritizing debt reduction over dividends or M&A; reinvestment in specialty chemicals and supply chain resilience; no new dividend policy mentioned
risks & watch-items: Currency volatility (EUR, JPY, BRL depreciation); high interest rates increasing finance costs; geopolitical instability (Ukraine conflict); weather disruptions affecting crop demand; potential margin compression if feedstock prices fall sharply; regulatory bans in Europe; working capital intensity in Brazil
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, and focused on quality growth; management emphasizes margin expansion over volume, operational efficiency, and debt reduction; tone is proactive on sustainability and value unlocking; acknowledges macro headwinds but projects resilience and execution strength
non-obvious takeaways: UPL is the least China-dependent major global agrochemical player due to deep backward integration in India; working capital buildup is strategic (sell closer to season) not operational inefficiency; factoring remains flat at $1.6B despite sales growth, indicating disciplined receivables management; sustainability loans were refinanced at lower spreads but benchmark rate hikes offset gains; Kudos acquisition is a low-cost entry into high-margin specialty chemicals with existing infrastructure

themes.title: Agrochemicals & crop-input cycle recovery
themes.need: Crop-protection is recovering off a brutal trough, and Q1FY27 shows domestic branded volume decoupling from generic exports. RALLIS grew revenue only 7% yet lifted EBITDA 23% to a ~18.0% margin (+230bps) as domestic B2C rose 19% on +15% volume while exports COLLAPSED 28% (volume -35%) on Chinese pricing, and its seeds EBITDA margin went 26% to 30% on a rice/maize/millet mix versus price-controlled cotton - though PAT +31% is flattered by an INR 35cr employee-provision reversal of which INR 24cr is genuinely one-time, so normalise before extrapolating. The monsoon is the live variable: as of 8-Jul seasonal rainfall was ~15% below normal with kharif acreage ~21% below last year. SUMICHEM delivered record FY26 profitability; INSECTICID/DHANUKA/SHARDACROP ride premiumization + technicals; COROMANDEL/GNFC/CHAMBLFERT/GODREJAGRO add fertilizers + integrated agri.
themes.driver: Monsoon catch-up and kharif acreage recovery from ~21% below last year; domestic B2C volume against continued Chinese export price pressure; new molecule launches and biologicals scale-up.
